jobs.title: Senior Data Operations Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

The hardest part of building general-purpose robots is not the model. It is the data: real, dexterous, physical-world manipulation that does not live on the internet. Our unlock is a data-collection glove built to the exact geometry of our robot hand, unobtrusive enough that a person can wear it through a normal workday, so ordinary work becomes training data that transfers to the robot without loss. Paired with our own hardware, simulation, and models in one tight loop, that is the most scalable manipulation data engine in the world.

This is the role that runs that engine on the ground. You will own the system that turns stations, workforce, and facilities into one reliable operation, end to end, from the operator at the station to the accepted hour that lands in training. You will grow it from a single floor into a global, multi-shift operation that holds a world-class quality bar as it scales. We are looking for someone who has run data collection at scale and is hungry to do it again at the frontier of physical AI.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run the floor end to end. Own scheduling, operator utilization, station uptime, and the throughput that delivers accepted hours at the quality bar, every week.

 - Build the operator bench. Recruit, level, and develop operators and the senior operators who run shifts, until the team is deep enough for multiple shifts and multiple sites.

 - Hold one standard everywhere. Make every floor we run and every partner site collect to the same playbook, the same metrics, and the same bar.

 - Turn problems into process. Root-cause what slows the floor and ship the SOPs, layouts, and tooling that make the next site ramp faster than the last.

 - Partner on quality and annotation. Work hand in hand with the Quality and Process and Annotation functions so collected hours convert cleanly into training-ready data.

 - Stand up partner-site collection. Rehearse and run the mock-runs and first deployments that bring partner operators onto our gear.

 - Report the truth. Build the reporting that tells the company, honestly, what we collected, at what quality, and at what cost.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You have built data collection at scale, and it shows. You have run a teleoperation, glove, or human-data operation at a frontier robotics lab, an embodied-AI company, or a top data operation, and you know the difference between hours collected and hours that actually train a model. There is a short list of places this work happens. If you have done it, we want to talk.

 - Throughput is in your blood. Scheduling, utilization, yield, and the hundred details of a working floor are second nature.

 - Quality is never optional. You have run an operation where the bar was real and measured, and you held it without slowing the line.

 - You run through walls. Bias for action, deep ownership, and a refusal to wait for permission. You see what needs doing and make it happen.

 - You build teams that win. You hire well, coach honestly, and people do their best work for you.

 - You work across sites and cultures. You are comfortable partnering with our teams and sites in Asia and Europe, and operating across time zones.




HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

 - Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

 - Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

 - Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

 - Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

 - Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

 - Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

 - A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

jobs.title: Business Development Manager
jobs.description:
Role Overview

You will own the customer side of our go to market motion, from identifying design partners to driving pilots through to commercial deployment. You will work directly with early customers, shape how our robotics systems are deployed in real environments, and convert early engagements into long term partnerships. This role sits at the intersection of product, engineering, and revenue.

Responsibilities

 - Identify, engage, and develop pipeline with early design partners across industries where robotics can create meaningful impact

 - Build deep relationships with early adopters to understand workflows, operational constraints, and real world problems

 - Drive customer engagements from initial outreach through pilot, deployment, and expansion

 - Own pilot to production conversion, including commercial discussions and deal execution

 - Translate customer insights into actionable feedback for product and engineering teams

 - Work closely with engineering to shape product direction based on real world usage

 - Lead early pilot deployments and customer evaluation programs

 - Navigate complex technical sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders

 - Build structured customer feedback loops that inform roadmap and prioritization

 - Support product demonstrations, proof of concept programs, and early customer trials

 - Develop use cases and deployment playbooks for robotics applications

 - Define pricing, packaging, and commercial structures for early deployments

 - Work closely with the Partnerships Lead to align ecosystem strategy with customer demand

 - Represent the voice of the customer internally across product, engineering, and leadership teams

Qualifications

 - Experience in customer-facing roles within robotics, autonomy, AI, or deep technology environments

 - Background in customer development, solutions engineering, product strategy, technical business development, or sales

 - Experience in management consulting or equivalent problem-solving roles, with exposure to operational or industrial systems

 - Experience at an early-stage or high-growth startup, ideally operating in 0→1 or pre-product environments

 - Strong technical fluency, able to engage directly with engineering teams and customers on system behavior, constraints, and deployment tradeoffs

 - Proven ability to own pipeline, drive deals end-to-end, and close complex, technical engagements

 - Track record working across product and engineering to translate real-world customer needs into shipped systems

 - Experience selling into or deploying within operational environments such as manufacturing, logistics, or industrial settings

 - Comfortable leading ambiguous, high-stakes engagements with early adopters and shaping the product in parallel

 - High agency and execution focus, able to operate independently and drive outcomes without defined playbooks

 - Strong communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills

jobs.title: Head of Marketing
jobs.description:
WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Translate research and engineering progress into clear external communication

 - Partner closely with founders, business teams and engineers to prepare milestone announcements, launch materials, and ecosystem updates

 - Build and maintain a coherent public narrative around Genesis’s

 - Design and execute our presence at major AI, robotics, autonomy, and deep tech conferences

 - Produce high-fidelity system demonstrations that accurately reflect real-world performance

 - Run lab visits, partner briefings, and technical press sessions

 - Create long-form technical explainers, talks, and written materials grounded in engineering accuracy

 - Support recruiting by clearly articulating the company’s mission, roadmap, and standards

 - Establish editorial and visual standards that reflect rigor and discipline

 - Build the marketing function from zero and hire selectively as the company scales

 - Operate hands-on without layers of support or predefined processes




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Required: Experience in a hardware, robotics, autonomy, aerospace, or similarly technical environment

 - Required: 0→1 startup experience building something from scratch in a high-uncertainty setting

 - Strong ability to communicate complex systems clearly without oversimplification

 - Experience supporting major technical launches or public milestones

 - Comfort working directly with engineers and research teams

 - High ownership, autonomy, and bias for execution

 - Strong judgment around credibility, confidentiality, and technical precision

 - Ability to operate independently without structured playbooks

 - Ideally: Experience at an autonomy, aerospace, robotics, or frontier hardware company

 - Ideally: Experience communicating safety, reliability, and deployment readiness

 - Ideally: Experience running technical demonstrations or field events

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Supply Chain (Robot Production)
jobs.description:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

Every part that goes into our robot: who makes it, at what price, on what lead time, to what quality. You build the supplier base for production, develop domestic sources for the sub-systems that need them, and make sure the line never waits on a part. You start with a bill of materials, a design team and a few suppliers; you end with a qualified, dual-sourced supply chain that supports production with our manufacturing partner at a cost that comes down with volume.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build the supplier base: source, qualify and manage suppliers for machined and cast structures, gears and actuators, motors, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two sources for every critical sub-system.

 - Develop domestic suppliers where the product and our customers require them, and manage the content requirements that come with selling into regulated markets.

 - Own the commercial side: RFQs, should-cost and total-cost models, piece price and tooling negotiation, long-term agreements, payment and warranty terms; work with Legal on supplier agreements and with Finance on the cost roadmap.

 - Sit in design reviews from the start: flag long-lead, single-source and high-risk parts before design freeze; bring supplier capability into the design.

 - Own clear-to-build and the plan: every unit on the schedule has a complete kit before it starts; a rolling plan the line, the partner and the suppliers all see; capacity planning with suppliers ahead of demand; inventory accuracy and safety stock by part class.

 - Own the BOM in production: cost roll-ups by phase, engineering change control with the design team and Manufacturing Engineering, cost-down from pilot to volume.

 - Build the supplier quality loop with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality: first article and PPAP where it applies, incoming inspection, supplier scorecards and quarterly reviews, corrective action and recovery.

 - Run logistics: inbound, between our facility and our partner's, import and export paperwork with Legal, spares and service parts.

 - Stand up the systems as we grow: part numbering, BOM control, MRP, supplier portal; the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, PPV, inventory) and the readout to leadership.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You have built a supplier base for a hardware product going into production, not managed one handed to you.

 - Deep experience with machined and cast metal parts, gears or actuators, motors, PCBAs and harnesses, and the suppliers who make them; you read drawings and GD&T.

 - You have developed new suppliers in new regions and qualified them to a standard.

 - Strong commercial record: you have negotiated price, tooling and terms with suppliers and contract manufacturers and closed long-term agreements.

 - You are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and cost roll-ups, and comfortable with the people who design the product.

 - 8 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or supplier development for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what the systems look like at scale, and experience leading people; engineering degree preferred.

 - Bonus: robotics or automotive; contract manufacturer selection and transition; import and export compliance; APICS or CPSM.




WORKING CONDITIONS

Office and production environments; travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 30%.




HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

 - Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

 - Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

 - Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

 - Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

 - Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

 - Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

 - A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.
